title: Route 4 after dark: what changes on 10 January, and what doesn't

speaker.name: Marta Lindqvist
speaker.about: transport officer at a town council, presenting at a public meeting; careful, answers every setup question and pastes one note

notes: Regular trips: you can make a standing booking, for example the same pick-up every weekday after a shift. Set it up once by phone or in the app and it repeats until you cancel it.
interview: The drivers who work evening Route 4 today are being offered the Hop driving jobs with Tarn Mobility on the same pay. Nobody is being made redundant.
The booking phone line is answered by real people from 08:00 to 01:30 every day, with two call handlers in the evening. You do not need a smartphone or an email address to book.
Aldercote is left out because it is in the neighbouring district and Northfell District Council has not agreed to pay its share. We are still talking to them.
On bank holidays Hop runs to the Sunday hours.

audience.name: Dorothy Pike
audience.about: 78, retired school secretary, no smartphone, takes Route 4 home from choir on Thursdays; anxious, polite, long-winded
asks: Good evening. I do not have a smart phone, only an old mobile my grandson set up and a landline, and I go home on the Route 4 bus from choir every Thursday night after 7pm. Does this mean I will not be able to get home any more after the 10th of January? I am rather worried.
Thank you, that is a relief if I can ring up to book. Will my bus pass still work on the Hop minibus or do I have to pay now? I only have the free pass and I never carry much cash.

My neighbour says those phone lines are always engaged. What happens if I ring and nobody answers, or I cant get through, and I am stood outside the church hall in the dark on a Thursday night? Is there somebody I can ask or somewhere I can go to book in person?

audience.name: Callum Reyes
audience.about: 41, public transport planner at the county council; precise, tests the details, notices when two slides disagree
asks: Slide 11 says £32,000 saved but slide 12 says about £28,700 if trips stay flat. Which figure should people quote?

asks.q: Is the 9 in 10 within 15 minutes an actual contractual KPI on Tarn Mobility with financial penalties, or just an aspiration? Slide 9 says it's an aim, not a guarantee.

asks: What exactly would end the trial early? Is there a defined failure criterion, or just thresholds nobody has published?

audience.name: Lucía Fernández
audience.about: 34, hospital cleaner on late shifts that end at 00:45; types fast in Spanish with typos and abbreviations
asks: salgo del hospital a las 00:45 entre semana, hay bus pa volver a casa??

asks.q: si el servicio acaba a las 00:30, q hacen los q salimos a esa hora?? lo van a ampliar??

asks: puedo reservar el mismo viaje para todos los dias de una vez o tengo q llamar cada vez??

audience.name: Graham Tott
audience.about: 63, retired lorry driver, distrusts the council; arrived late and wrongly believes the number 4 is being scrapped all day
asks: So you're scrapping the number 4 altogether and calling it progress. How are people meant to get to work in the morning?
Right, so the daytime bus stays. Fine. Are the bus drivers losing their jobs though, yes or no?
Be honest, is this Hop thing actually going to work or is it just another council vanity project?

audience.name: Jay
audience.about: 16, dragged along by a parent, bored; pokes at the question box, then asks what matters to a teenager
asks: can u do my geography hw wats the longest river in england and how do rivers form
whats the latest i can get home on a saturday

asks.q: can i bring my bike on it

replies.answer: Folding bikes, folded up, yes. Full-size bikes, no: the minibuses have no rack.

It is in the contract. Tarn Mobility must pick up at least 85% of bookings within 15 minutes each month; in any month below that it loses 5% of that month's fee. 9 in 10 is what we are aiming for on top.
